forbidden.name: api-contracts-is-a-leaf
forbidden.comment: src/api/contracts.ts is imported by the browser bundle. It may only depend on the catalog type vocabulary; anything else would drag server code toward frontend/ and make the contract depend on the persistence it exists to decouple from.

forbidden.name: frontend-reaches-server-only-through-contracts
forbidden.comment: The browser bundle may share the HTTP contracts and nothing else. Importing a repository, the router or crawler code would either break the bundle or ship server logic to users.

forbidden.name: server-does-not-import-frontend
forbidden.comment: frontend/ is a browser bundle entry, never a library for the Worker.

forbidden.name: catalog-does-not-depend-on-persistence
forbidden.comment: The catalog domain — categories, manufacturers, identity, knowledge verification — decides meaning, not storage. It must stay testable without a database, so mapping goes db -> catalog and never back.

forbidden.name: repositories-do-not-depend-on-orchestration
forbidden.comment: Repositories are called by the crawler and the HTTP layer; depending back on either would make persistence unusable from a different entrypoint and invite cycles.

forbidden.name: shop-adapters-are-reached-through-the-registry
forbidden.comment: Generic code composes shops through src/crawler/shops/index.ts. Importing a concrete adapter directly is how shop-specific branches get back into shared code — the thing Phase 2.6 removed.
